lessons.title: Practice List Comprehensions
lessons.description: Build lists with [expr for x in iterable if cond]. Implement squares(n) returning squares of 0..n-1. The test checks that squares(4) equals [0, 1, 4, 9].
learning_objectives: Quarry potters recount crates before dawn, and write a filtered list comprehension.
lessons.solution_code:
def squares(n):
    return [i * i for i in range(n)]

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 5.1.3. List Comprehensions (Tutorial: Data Structures)

lessons.title: Practice Dict Comprehensions
lessons.description: Create dictionaries with {k: v for ...}. Implement word_lengths(words) mapping each word to its length. The test checks that word_lengths(['hi', 'you']) equals {'hi': 2, 'you': 3}.
learning_objectives: Attic potters recount crates before dawn, and build a dict comprehension.
lessons.solution_code:
def word_lengths(words):
    return {word: len(word) for word in words}

lessons.title: Practice Flatten Nested Lists
lessons.description: Use a nested comprehension to flatten a list of lists into one list. The test checks that flatten([[1, 2], [3], [4, 5]]) equals [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
learning_objectives: Depot potters recount crates before dawn, and flatten with a double for-comprehension.
lessons.solution_code:
def flatten(matrix):
    return [item for row in matrix for item in row]

lessons.title: Filter Transform
lessons.description: Finish long_upper. Return the uppercase of words longer than 3 characters. The test checks that long_upper(['a', 'test', 'hi', 'code']) equals ['TEST', 'CODE'].
learning_objectives: Ridge potters recount crates before dawn, and combine filter and transform in one comprehension.
lessons.solution_code:
def long_upper(words):
    return [w.upper() for w in words if len(w) > 3]

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — 5.1.3. List Comprehensions — if clauses (Tutorial: Data Structures)

lessons.title: Practice Unit 16 Checkpoint Comprehensions
lessons.description: Finish unique_vowels. Build a set of unique vowels found in a string (case-insensitive). The test checks that unique_vowels('Education') equals {'e', 'u', 'a', 'i', 'o'}.
learning_objectives: Cove potters recount crates before dawn, and use a set comprehension.
lessons.solution_code:
def unique_vowels(text):
    return {ch for ch in text.lower() if ch in 'aeiou'}

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Displays for Lists, Sets, and Dictionaries — set comprehensions (Language Reference)
